newsitem.title: FRANCE: French consumer gloom worsens, job fears rise.
newsitem.headline: French consumer gloom worsens, job fears rise.

text.p: French household sentiment worsened in September, despite a government tax-cutting package meant to revive consumer spending and economic growth, a survey by national statistics institute INSEE released on Thursday showed.
INSEE said its overall confidence index fell to minus 37 from 35 in July.
Consumer's views on the outlook for unemployment worsened further, showing a level of 79 for those expecting joblessness to rise, compared to 77 in July and just 30 in October 1995.
French unemployment reached a record 12.6 percent in August, hitting 3.09 million people.
Despite the tax-cutting package, consumers' views on whether now was a good time to spend deteriorated, while they judged that it was a better time to save.

The government said on September 5 that the government planned to cut income taxes by a net 18 billion francs next year, in a measure designed to offset the impact on the economy of a spending-cutting budget announced later in the month.
But the tax cut plans were widely attacked in the French press, which said other increases on excise duties and local authority taxes would minimise the impact of the tax cuts.
The overall confidence index hit a trough of minus 38 in May this year compared to minus 30 in October last year.
The overall index covers views on past and future living standards, past and future personal finances and on whether it would a good time to spend, but does not include sentiment on unemployment.
